chapters.name: Chapter 1: Seeing and answering your customers

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Mapping the customer journey
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Draw a customer journey map and mark the weakest moments.
This lesson builds toward: For a real or practice organization, you will draw a customer journey map from discover to after and mark the three weakest moments, with what the customer does and feels at each step.
A customer journey map lists every step a person goes through with you, in order: discover (how they find you), ask (first contact), decide, buy or receive the service, and after (follow-up, review, coming back).
At each step, write what the customer does, what they feel, and what could go wrong. For a food bank: a family finds the hours online, calls with a question, waits in line, receives food, and wonders when to come back.
AI can help you see steps you missed. Ask: "I run a home repair business. List every step a customer goes through from first search to after the job, and what could frustrate them at each step." Then compare with what you see every day.
Step by step:
- List the steps: discover, ask, decide, buy or receive, after.
- For each step, write what the customer does and feels.
- Ask AI what could frustrate them at each step.
- Mark the three weakest moments.
Words to know:
- Customer experience: how people feel at every point they deal with an organization.
- Journey map: a step-by-step picture of a customer's experience.
- Touchpoint: any moment a customer deals with you: a call, a post, a visit, an email.
Try it now: Draw a journey map for a real or practice organization with at least five steps. Use AI to find frustrations you missed and mark the three weakest moments.
You can now map a customer journey and find where the experience breaks down.

check.q: Which step of the customer journey is about follow-up, reviews and coming back?
check.why: The "after" step covers follow-up, reviews and return visits.

check.q: AI lists frustrations for your cleaning business's journey map. What do you do with the list?
options: Copy it as your final map
Compare it with what you see every day and keep what is true
check.why: AI can point out steps you missed, but your daily experience confirms them.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Writing fast, warm replies with AI
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Build reply templates with AI for the questions you get most.
This lesson builds toward: Given your five most common questions and the true facts, you will write AI-drafted reply templates in your own voice, personalized and fact-checked before each use.
Fast replies matter. A template is a ready-made reply you adjust for each person. AI can draft templates in your voice in seconds.
Give the AI context: your organization, your tone and the facts. "Write a friendly reply for a barbershop to the question 'Do you take walk-ins?' Facts: walk-ins welcome Tuesday to Thursday, appointments needed Friday and Saturday, book at our website. Under 50 words."
Always personalize before sending: use the person's name, answer exactly what they asked, and check the facts. A reply that sounds like a robot or gets the hours wrong hurts more than it helps.
Step by step:
- List your five most common questions.
- Give AI your tone and the true facts for each.
- Ask for a short, friendly template.
- Save the templates in a document.
- Personalize and check facts each time you use one.
Words to know:
- Template: a ready-made reply you adjust for each person.
- Personalize: change a message so it fits the specific person.
Try it now: Use AI to write templates for your three most common customer questions. Save them, then personalize one for a made-up customer.
You can now build and personalize AI-drafted reply templates.

check.q: What should you give AI so a reply template is accurate?
options: Your tone and the true facts
check.why: Your tone and the real facts let AI draft a reply that is right and sounds like you.

check.q: A customer named Ana asks about parking. You have a template. What do you do?
options: Send the template exactly as it is
Send her every template you have
Add her name, answer exactly what she asked and check the facts
check.why: Personalize and check facts each time you use a template.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Answering reviews and complaints
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Reply to a positive review, a negative review and a complaint calmly and helpfully.
This lesson builds toward: Given a positive review, a negative review and a complaint, you will write calm, helpful replies using listen, apologize, solve, follow up, with no private details in any public reply.
Reviews are public, so your reply is for everyone reading, not only the reviewer. Thank people for positive reviews and mention something specific. For negative reviews, stay calm, apologize for their experience, do not argue, and offer to fix it offline with a phone number or email.
For complaints, use a simple pattern: listen, apologize, solve, follow up. Ask AI: "Help me reply to this complaint. Pattern: acknowledge, apologize, offer this fix: [your fix], invite them to contact [email]."
Never share private details in a public reply, such as appointment dates, health information or what someone bought. Never post fake reviews or pay for them. If a review contains threats or false claims, follow the platform's reporting process.
Step by step:
- Read the review twice and wait if you feel upset.
- Thank them (positive) or acknowledge and apologize (negative).
- Offer a specific fix or a way to talk offline.
- Keep private details out of public replies.
- Follow up to make sure it was solved.
Words to know:
- Review: a public comment and rating about a business.
- Offline: away from the public page, such as by phone or private email.
Try it now: Write AI-assisted replies to one positive review, one negative review and one complaint (real or made up). Check each for calm tone and no private details.
You can now answer reviews and complaints calmly, helpfully and without sharing private details.

check.q: What should a reply to a positive review include?
options: A thank-you and something specific from their review
check.why: Thank people and mention something specific so the reply feels real.

check.q: A client posts that your clinic made them wait an hour. How do you reply in public?
options: Acknowledge it, apologize and offer to talk offline by phone or email
Explain their appointment details and medical reason for the wait
check.why: Stay calm, apologize, offer to fix it offline and keep private details out.

chapters.name: Chapter 2: Learning from feedback and improving

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Analyzing feedback with AI
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Use AI to sort customer comments into themes and find the top issues.
This lesson builds toward: Given at least 15 customer comments with private details removed, you will sort the comments into themes with AI and rank the top three issues, after spot-checking a few comments in each theme.
Feedback hides in many places: reviews, surveys, emails, social comments and notes from staff. Reading it all by hand takes hours. AI can sort it in minutes.
Collect at least 15 comments in a document. Remove names, phone numbers and other private details. Then ask: "Sort these comments into themes. For each theme, count how many comments mention it, say if it is positive or negative, and give one example quote."
Check the AI's work: read a few comments in each theme to confirm they belong there. AI can miscount or merge different issues. The result is your top issues list, ranked by how often they come up and how much they hurt the experience.
Step by step:
- Collect at least 15 comments from reviews, surveys and emails.
- Remove names and private details.
- Ask AI to sort them into themes with counts and examples.
- Spot-check a few comments per theme.
- Rank the top three issues.
Words to know:
- Feedback: what customers tell you about their experience.
- Theme: a topic that comes up again and again.
- Sentiment: whether a comment is positive, negative or neutral.
Try it now: Gather at least 15 real or sample comments, remove private details, and have AI sort them into themes. Spot-check the results and list your top three issues.
You can now turn a pile of customer comments into a ranked list of top issues.

check.q: Why spot-check the themes AI creates?
options: AI can miscount or merge different issues
check.why: Reading a few comments per theme catches AI miscounts and merged issues.

check.q: Eight comments mention slow replies and two mention parking. Which do you rank higher?
options: Slow replies, because more people mention it
check.why: Rank issues by how often they come up and how much they hurt.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Personalizing service without losing trust
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use AI to personalize messages while protecting customer privacy and staying honest.
This lesson builds toward: For a thank-you, reminder or follow-up message, you will write a personalized template with placeholders that protects privacy and stays honest, only to people who agreed to hear from you, with a way to reach a person.
Personal touches make people feel valued: a birthday discount, a reminder before a client's next appointment, or a thank-you note to a donor that mentions the program they supported.
AI can help write these messages at scale from a template. Give it only the details it needs, like a first name and the service type, not full records. Use your own customer system or email tool to merge names in, rather than pasting customer lists into a general AI tool.
Be honest: if a chatbot or AI answers customers, say so. Make it easy to reach a person. Only message people who agreed to hear from you, and make it easy to opt out.
Step by step:
- Choose one personal moment: a thank-you, reminder or follow-up.
- Have AI write a template with placeholders like [First name].
- Fill in names using your own email or customer tool.
- Say clearly when a customer is talking with AI.
- Always offer a way to reach a person.
Words to know:
- Placeholder: a marker like [First name] that gets replaced with real details.
- Opt out: choose to stop getting messages.
Try it now: Write a personalized thank-you or follow-up template with AI using placeholders. Check that it asks for no private details and offers a way to reach a person.
You can now personalize customer messages with AI while protecting privacy and staying honest.

check.q: What is the safest way to send a thank-you note to 200 donors?
options: Use a template with [First name] and merge names in your own email tool
Paste the full donor list into a free AI tool
Write each note by hand without checking
Post all their names on social media
check.why: Merge names in your own tool so the donor list never goes into a general AI tool.

check.q: Your website chatbot answers customer questions. What must you add?
options: Nothing; customers prefer not to know
A clear note that it is AI and a way to reach a person
check.why: Being honest that it is AI and offering a person builds trust.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Turning insights into a 30-day improvement plan
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Turn your top issues into a 30-day plan with owners and measures.
This lesson builds toward: Given your top three issues, you will create a 30-day improvement plan, with one action, one owner and one measure for each issue.
Insights only matter if something changes. For each of your top three issues, choose one action you can take in 30 days. Example: "Customers say they wait too long for quotes" becomes "Send every quote within 24 hours using an AI-drafted quote template."
Give each action an owner and a measure: a number that will show if it worked, such as average reply time, review rating, repeat visits or complaints per week.
Tell customers what you changed: "You told us, we listened." After 30 days, check the measures, keep what worked and pick the next issue.
Step by step:
- Write one action for each top issue.
- Give each action an owner.
- Choose one measure for each.
- Record the starting number.
- Check again after 30 days and share what changed.
Words to know:
- Insight: a useful understanding that comes from studying information.
- Measure: a number that shows whether a change worked.
Try it now: Final task: write a 30-day improvement plan for your top three issues with an action, owner, measure and starting number for each. Add it to your journey map, templates and feedback summary to complete your customer experience kit.
You can now find, fix and measure customer experience problems with AI help.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Journey map Steps are missing, or the weakest moments are not marked. All five steps with what the customer does and feels, and three weakest moments marked. Each weak moment links to real feedback or a staff observation. Reply templates Fewer than five templates, or a template has wrong facts. Five templates (question, positive review, negative review, complaint, follow-up) with true facts and a warm tone. Each template has placeholders and a note on what to personalize. Review and complaint replies A reply argues, blames or shares private details. Replies are calm, apologize where needed and offer a fix or a way to talk offline. Includes a follow-up step to check the problem was solved. Feedback summary Fewer than 15 comments, or names left in. At least 15 comments with private details removed, sorted into themes and the top three issues ranked. Shows which themes were spot-checked and any AI mistakes fixed. 30-day plan Actions have no owner or measure. One action, owner and measure for each top issue, with a starting number. Includes how customers will be told what changed. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: What is a measure in an improvement plan?
options: A number that shows if the action worked
The date you started the business
check.why: A measure is a number, like average reply time, that shows whether the action worked.

check.q: Customers say they cannot find your hours. What is a good 30-day action?
options: Wait to see if it gets better
Ask AI to write reviews about your hours
Post the hours on every page and profile, with an owner and a measure
check.why: Each top issue gets one clear action, an owner and a measure.
